ROW.COLUMN: (ML/CB) Patterns of Sequentially Numbered Checks, Monetary Instruments

Money launderers seeking to place funds into the banking system may purchase, or employ agents to purchase, large numbers of monetary instruments at various locations, such as bank branches or postal offices. One typology is to purchase a string of money orders that aggregate to just under the cash log threshold of USD 3,000 (or specific jurisdiction equivalent), or the currency-reporting threshold of USD 10,000 (or specific jurisdiction equivalent). These instruments are deposited into another, typically non-US institution, and then cleared through that institution's correspondent account with a US bank. Or, the funds may be deposited in this manner into domestic accounts (retail and commercial), then transferred to other accounts and eventually out of the institution. This scenario identifies accounts, customers, households, client banks, or external entities that have substantial risk as a result of the placement of large numbers of sequentially numbered monetary instruments (such as money orders) into the banking system.

There are two main datasets in this scenario. The first selects client-banks which have MI-transactions for the look back period and at least one transaction for the frequency period. This dataset is the start of the sequence. The second dataset selects all MI-transactions for the look-back period. One more dataset is used for the properly end of the pattern. The sort order of the datasets in the pattern includes the focal entity, the product code, name, routing number and serial number of the monetary instruments of the transactions. All monetary instruments are divided on two types: true-sequenced events (when conditions for a single episode are met); false-sequenced events (when conditions for a single episode are not met).
For the true-sequenced events aggregate values are counted. In the end of the sequence (a record for another Focal Entity or End-of-Stream event) conditions for episodes are checked, and if necessary the match is raised.
